newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers seek inexpensive spot cover.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers seek inexpensive spot cover.

text.p: German cotton consumers are looking for spot cover as prices have eased in line with lower world market prices, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
New York cotton futures last week set new lows on high U.S. Department of Agriculture planting intentions data for 1997/98.
A relatively lower dollar values against the mark also offered savings.
Buyers favoured Central Asian cotton because of its price discount and their availability via the Baltic States.

The Exchange reported upland turnover for 1997 dates in Central Asian standards 1-4, West African and Chadian material, Zimbabwean and Paraguayan cotton as well as Israel-Acala and East African roller ginned cotton.
Cotton stocks as of April 4 totalled 44,876 bales, down from 134,871 bales a year earlier.
In the long staple sector, the Exchange reported 1997 trades in Central Asian grades, Sudan-Shambat and Israel-Pima.
